en.headline: Police to activate AI facial recognition on SmartView network from Monday
en.dek: Commissioner Joe Chow said the system would help identify people even if they wore masks, serving as protection for law-abiding residents and a deterrent against crime.
body: Hong Kong police will switch on artificial intelligence-powered facial recognition across the SmartView surveillance camera network from Monday, Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming said on Saturday.

Speaking after a passing-out parade at the Police College, Chow said the technology could identify individuals even if they used masks or other methods to avoid detection. He described it as a safeguard for law-abiding citizens and a form of surveillance for those who commit crimes.

Police have previously outlined two uses: retrospective searches of footage for a person of interest, and real-time alerts when a missing person or wanted individual appears on camera. The force has said searches require approval from an inspector or higher and are limited to crime prevention, public safety and related purposes.
SmartView, launched in 2024, already covers high-footfall and higher-crime areas with thousands of cameras. The force aims to expand the network substantially in the coming years.

zh.headline: 警方周一在銳眼監控網絡啟用人工智能人臉識別
zh.dek: 警務處處長周一鳴表示，技術即使有人戴口罩亦可協助識別，旨在保障守法市民並對犯罪起阻嚇作用。
body: 警務處處長周一鳴周六表示，警方將於周一在「銳眼」閉路電視監控網絡啟用人工智能人臉識別功能。
周一鳴在警察學院結業禮後向傳媒表示，有關技術即使有人佩戴口罩或其他方法逃避偵測，仍可協助識別身份。他形容這是對守法市民的保障，亦是對企圖犯罪者的監察。
警方早前已說明系統主要有兩種用法：事後翻查特定影像以搜尋目標人物，以及即時追蹤，當失蹤者或通緝人士出現在鏡頭前時發出警報。警方表示，每次搜尋須由督察或以上職級批准，用途限於罪案偵測、公共安全等範疇。
「銳眼計劃」於2024年推出，已在高人流及罪案黑點裝設大量鏡頭。警方計劃未來數年大幅擴展網絡覆蓋。
